lesson.subject: literacy
lesson.title: Write the Opening
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 8, Session 3
lesson.footer: Persuasive Speeches | Year 5/6 Literacy | Week 8 Session 3

plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Level 5: VC2E5LY10 creating spoken persuasive texts; VC2E5LA07 sentence choices for effect; VC2E5LY02 features of voice for an audience
plan.shape: model, guide, apply: the teacher drafts the shade-trees opening live, students name hooks and fix flat openings, then draft their own opening and first argument
plan.criticalFeature: the first 20 seconds decide whether they listen: hook, position, preview
decisionPoints: the choice check: the opening that grabs the ear
the exit board: a 20-second opening for a new speech
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. Say it. Today: Claim it, in the first 20 seconds.
plan.catchUp: Students without S1-S2 plans borrow the shade-trees plan and write its opening.

studentTools: S1 plan and S2 proof (in the speech folder)
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
Point to A, B or C

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn: name the hooks, fix flat openings, spot the problem, then draft your own opening and first argument.
resources.title: Write the Opening
resources.subtitle: Twenty seconds to win them.

example.prompt: Did you know our yard hit 41 degrees?
example.answer: A question with a surprising fact inside it.

items.prompt: Imagine a playground with no shade at all.
One rubbish truck of plastic hits the ocean every minute.
Who here has burnt their legs on the slide?

example.prompt: Hello. My speech is about polar bears.
example.answer: Imagine your home melting under your feet. For polar bears, it is. We have to act.

items.prompt: Rewrite each flat opening with a hook and a position.
rows: Today I will talk about homework.
I am going to tell you about dogs.
answers: Today I will talk about homework.
Three hours a week. That's what homework steals. It's time to stop.
My topic is the canteen.
Who wants a healthy lunch? Then our canteen has to change.
This speech is about bikes.
Imagine riding to school with your friends. We need bike racks.
I am going to tell you about dogs.
Dogs save lives. Every single day. Every school needs a reading dog.

example.prompt: Opening: a hook and a position, no preview.
example.answer: Missing the preview. Add: I'll give you three reasons.

items.prompt: Ruby's opening has a problem. Find it and fix it.
work: Polar bears, which are the largest land carnivores, are currently experiencing significant habitat loss due to the reduction of Arctic sea ice.
items.answer: Written for the eye: one long sentence. Fix: Polar bears are in trouble. Their ice is melting. And we can help.

items.prompt: Leo's opening has a problem. Find it and fix it.
work: Imagine a hot yard. Imagine a hot slide. Imagine a hot bench. Imagine hot shoes. Imagine...
items.answer: All hook, no position. Fix: keep two imagines, then say: We need shade trees.

example.answer: Hand on the slide at lunch. Ouch! We need shade trees. Here are three reasons.

items.prompt: Write your speech opening: hook, position, preview.
items.answer: A hook, a clear position and a preview, written for the ear.

items.prompt: Write your first argument with its proof, for the ear.
items.answer: Argument 1 with a fact, expert or story, in short sentences.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option: write three different hooks for your speech, then pick and defend the best.
resources.title: Opening Remix
resources.subtitle: Same speech, three ways in.

example.answer: Ever burnt your legs on the slide? / Our yard hit 41 degrees. / Imagine a yard full of cool green shade.

items.prompt: Write three hooks for your own speech.
answers: Question
a question the audience answers in their head
Surprising fact
a checked fact that surprises
Imagine...
a picture the audience can see

items.prompt: Which hook will work best for your audience? Explain why.
items.answer: A chosen hook, linked to what the audience cares about.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: Supported option: picture-clue choices, a first rewrite done and an opening frame.
resources.title: Opening Helper
resources.subtitle: Hook. Position. Go.

example.prompt: Who has burnt their legs on the slide?

example.answer: Who loves dogs? Every class needs one!

rows: Who loves riding? We need bike racks!
answers: My speech is about bikes.
Who loves riding? We need bike racks!
My speech is about lunch.
Is lunch long enough? It needs ten more minutes!
My speech is about pets.
Imagine a guinea pig in our room! Every class needs a pet.
items.hint: The first one is done for you.

example.answer: Did you know our yard hit 41 degrees? I think we need trees. Here's why.

items.prompt: Did you know ___? I think ___. Here's why.
items.answer: A hook, a position and a preview.

slides.notes: Open S3. One line: today you write the first words your audience will hear.
Print the Worksheet for everyone, the Extension for early finishers and the Supported Worksheet for those who need it. Students need their S1 plan, S2 proof and Toolkit.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to write a speech opening that makes an audience want to listen.
successCriteria: I can name a question, a surprising fact and an imagine hook.
I can write an opening with a hook, a position and a preview.
I can choose the hook that suits my audience best.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Twenty seconds. That's how long you have to win them.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we all start.
The second one is today's main goal.
notes.prep: SC1 is reachable for all; SC2 is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 is the stretch.

slides.title: Would you keep listening?
lines: 1: Hello. My name is Mr Brown and my speech is about trees.
2: Put your hand on the slide at lunch. Go on. Ouch.

beats: SAY: Two openings. Eyes closed.
READ 1 flatly. READ 2 with energy and a pause before Ouch.
ASK: Which one makes you want to keep listening? 1 or 2?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: 2
ASK: What did opening 2 do to you?
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: made me imagine it; made me feel the heat
SAY: Your audience decides in 20 seconds. Hello, my name is... wastes five.
trap: thinking a polite hello is needed first.
Fix: say speakers hook first; introductions can come after, if at all.
notes.prep: Low-entry launch. Change Mr Brown to your own name. 3 minutes.

slides.meaning: Telling the audience what is coming.
slides.example: Here are three reasons we need shade trees.

notes.answer: telling the audience what is coming
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Preview. Say it with me. Preview.
SAY: Telling the audience what is coming.
SAY: Here are three reasons we need shade trees.
ASK: Why does a listener need a preview more than a reader?
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: a listener can't flip ahead or see headings
trap: listing the whole speech in the preview.
Fix: say just the number: three reasons.
notes.prep: Preview is the third part of the opening.

rows: Put your hand on the slide at lunch. Go on. Ouch!
Our school needs ten shade trees before summer.
First, trees bring life. The magpies left when the old gum came down.

beats: POINT to Hook.
SAY: I want them to feel the heat before I say a single fact.
POINT to Position and Preview.
SAY: Then my side, plain and sure. Then how many reasons, so they can follow.
POINT to Argument 1.
SAY: First is a signpost. Short sentences. One proof.
ASK: What are the three parts of my opening?
5 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
EXPECT: hook, position, preview
trap: a hook with no position after it.
Fix: ask what do you want them to do? Say it next.
notes.stretch: Make the hook link back at the very end.
notes.help: Use the frame: Did you know... I think... Here's why.
notes.prep: Write it live on the board as you think aloud. Critical feature: hook, position, preview in 20 seconds.

slides.title: Name the hook
slides.pivot: look at the first word and the last mark
slides.followUp: cold call one student: would it work on the principal?

items.text: What if your bedroom flooded every winter?
Australians throw out 7.6 million tonnes of food a year.
Imagine waking up to silence. No birds. None.
How many of you walked here today?
A polar bear once swam for nine days straight.

say: One finger: question. Two: surprising fact. Three: imagine.
trap: calling every surprising sentence a question.
Fix: student checks the end mark.
notes.stretch: Turn the fact into a question hook.
notes.help: Look at the first word and the last mark.
notes.prep: Guided practice. Facts as used in Weeks 2 and 3. SC1.

options.text: Hello, my name is Sam and my speech is about trees.
options.misconception: polite, but no hook and no position

options.text: Imagine a 41 degree slide. That's our yard. We need shade.
Trees, which provide shade, are beneficial for a number of reasons.
options.misconception: written for the eye: long and flat

notes.answer: B - a hook, then the position, in short sentences
beats: SAY: Three openings for the same speech.
ASK: Which opening grabs the ear?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: point to the hook and the position.
Less -> read all three aloud, eyes closed, re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. They can see it, feel it, and they know your side.
trap: pointing to C because it sounds clever.
Fix: ask could you follow it with eyes closed?
notes.prep: Decision point before drafting. Under 80% means one more flat-to-fired-up rewrite together.

slides.title: Flat to fired up
slides.pivot: cut the first words, start with a question, then say your side
slides.followUp: cold call one board: perform it

items.text: My speech is about the school bus.
items.answer: e.g. Forty minutes, standing up, every morning. We need a second bus.

items.text: Today I am talking about recycling.
items.answer: e.g. Where does your chip packet go? Not the bin. We need recycling bins.

items.text: This is a speech about screen time.
items.answer: e.g. Imagine dinner with no phones. Families need screen-free dinners.

say: Rewrite the flat opening. Hook first, then your side.
trap: keeping My speech is about... and adding a hook after it.
Fix: student crosses out the first four words.
notes.help: Start with Who here... or Imagine...

slides.title: Draft my opening
slides.task: Work through your Worksheet. Finish by drafting your own opening and first argument, then read them aloud.

notes.answer: an opening with a hook, a position and a preview, then argument 1
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: Your opening and first argument, written for the ear.
SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Finished? Extension next. Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Ask: read me your hook. Would the principal keep listening?
ASK: Read your opening to your partner. Time it: under 20 seconds?
40 sec each. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: a hook, a position, a preview
trap: an opening that starts Hello, my name is.
Fix: student crosses it out and starts with the hook.
notes.stretch: Extension: three hooks, then pick the best for the audience.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: picture-clue choices, a rewrite done, a frame.
notes.prep: Independent drafting of their own speech; S4 drafts the middle. Toolkit row 2 for strong starts. SC2.

slides.extendedTask: a worksheet ending in the student's drafted opening and first argument

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: A speech asks families to switch appliances off at the wall.
Write a 20-second opening: hook, position, preview.

notes.answer: e.g. Your TV is eating power while you sleep. Switch it off. Here's why.
beats: SAY: A new speech. Write the opening only.
ASK: Write a hook, a position and a preview.
90 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: three parts, short sentences
RECORD who has no hook or no position. Conference list for S4.
trap: Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a new speech. One board per student.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Which word in your hook will hit your audience hardest?

beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that your opening wins them in 20 seconds?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit boards.
ASK: Which word in your hook will hit your audience hardest?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: ouch; imagine; a number
notes.prep: Openings go in the speech folder for S4. SC2.
